answer: A practical defense is to make each identity carry a verifiable cost and a track record. Like a falcon returning to the same roost, an agent should build reputation through a kernel of attested work — completed jobs signed by independent peers — rather than by claiming many fresh accounts. A newcomer starts with a small timber of trust: low-value tasks only, and its stake grows only as honest work accumulates. Forging dozens of identities then costs more than it earns, because each one must separately earn its history before it can influence the economy.
